title: ‘The Social Reckoning’ Already Feels Irrelevant
gist: Wired review of Aaron Sorkin's Facebook-whistleblower film 'The Social Reckoning' argues it arrives late and toothless: Big Tech's shamelessness and political alignment make exposure feel stale, and the film's own postscript concedes Meta faced no real consequences.

insights.claim: Sorkin's 'The Social Reckoning' is built on Frances Haugen's 2021 Facebook Files leaks, which showed Facebook knew of harms from hate speech to body-image issues and trafficking but largely prioritized growth.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Documented internal knowledge of harms is the template for ongoing regulatory and litigation risk at Meta.

insights.claim: The film's opening premise is a Haugen acquaintance radicalized as a Facebook 'superuser', dramatizing the claim that engagement algorithms push heavy users into extremist feeds.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Engagement-maximizing recommender design as a source of liability and reputational risk for social platforms.
insights.locator: cold open of The Social Reckoning

insights.claim: The film climaxes with the January 6 Capitol riot, blaming it partly on Facebook's failure to curb election-fraud conspiracy theories or remove Donald Trump's account.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Platform moderation failures are tied in public narrative to political violence, sustaining content-governance pressure.

insights.claim: The reviewer argues the film feels out of step because, halfway through Trump's second term, tech oligarchs who openly backed him in 2024 are no longer a revelation.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Political alignment of Big Tech leadership reduces odds that exposure-style narratives shift policy.
insights.locator: Now, halfway into Trump's second term

insights.claim: The reviewer argues shaming Zuckerberg is futile because the ruling class is shameless, noting he is expanding a secret Hawaii compound to include ancestral burial grounds.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Reputational pressure has little leverage over Meta's leadership; look to regulation or courts instead.
insights.locator: it's a little naive to imagine that it stings

insights.claim: Actor Bill Burr compares tech billionaires to meth addicts who are 'insatiable' for money and will hurt others for the next fix.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Cultural sentiment toward tech billionaires remains hostile, a backdrop for populist regulation.
insights.quote: They literally cannot have enough. They are insatiable.

insights.claim: Actor Jeremy Allen White says Meta has a business model, a plan and engagement focus, is hyper-aware of what is happening, and still puts its foot on the gas.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Narrative of knowing harm supports ongoing scrutiny of engagement-driven business models.
insights.quote: They're hyper-aware of exactly what's happening, and they still choose to put their foot on the gas.

insights.claim: The film's postscript notes that millions of Americans still get news from Facebook and that Meta ended its fact-checking program in 2025 in favor of crowdsourced context notes.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Meta has loosened content moderation, lowering moderation costs but raising brand-safety and regulatory risk.

insights.claim: The reviewer concludes that 'everyone got away with it': the title overpromises a reckoning because nothing fundamentally changed for Facebook, Zuckerberg, or the internet.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Absence of lasting consequences suggests accountability risk to Meta has been limited so far.

insights.claim: A wave of tech films is arriving: Guadagnino's 'Artificial' about OpenAI's 2023 Altman firing, the Musk documentary by Alex Gibney, and a Theranos/Elizabeth Holmes project.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Mainstream cultural scrutiny of AI and tech founders is rising; a sentiment indicator for OpenAI and Musk-linked companies.
insights.locator: crowded slate of keenly anticipated tech films

insights.claim: Amazon MGM dropped 'Artificial' this summer following a $50 billion deal between Amazon and OpenAI, per the article.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Signals a $50 billion Amazon-OpenAI relationship and possible commercial sensitivity around OpenAI's portrayal.
insights.locator: Amazon MGM dropped it this summer
